blocks.html: For most businesses selling in India, the WhatsApp Business API is the safer channel to lead with — it reaches customers on both Android and iPhone, has mature tooling, and proven conversational commerce. Rich Communication Services (RCS) is climbing fast on Android through Google and operators like Jio and Airtel, and it is genuinely strong for high-volume transactional messaging. The honest answer is rarely one or the other: run one as your primary engagement channel and use the second as a complementary layer where it is cheaper or lands more reliably.

This guide compares the two on the things that actually decide the sale — reach, cost, deliverability, sender trust, and the rich features that turn a message into an action. Ojiva AI runs both from one dashboard alongside Bulk SMS, so if you would rather see it against your own volumes, book a free demo and we will map it to how your team already handles customers. Conversations that convert start with picking the right channel for each job.

sections.heading: How the Two Channels Differ Where It Counts

blocks.html: Before the detail, it helps to see the core trade-offs side by side. Choosing a business messaging channel is really about matching each one's strengths to the job in front of you — broad two-way engagement on one side, guaranteed delivery for alerts on the other.

items.title: Where it reaches:
items.desc: one runs as an app across Android and iPhone; the other lives in the native Android texting app and is still maturing on iPhone.

items.title: How it is billed:
items.desc: one charges per delivered message by category, the other is priced per message by the operator or aggregator.

items.title: What happens on failure:
items.desc: one simply does not deliver if unavailable; the other quietly drops to plain SMS so the alert still lands.

items.title: How mature the tooling is:
items.desc: one has deep chatbot, catalog and payment flows today; the other's business tooling is newer but improving quickly.

sections.heading: What RCS Business Messaging Actually Is

blocks.html: RCS business messaging is the upgrade to plain SMS: a Google- and operator-backed standard that turns the default Android Messages app into a branded channel with a verified sender name and logo, rich cards, carousels, suggested replies and read receipts. It needs no app install — it runs inside the phone's own texting app and drops back to SMS when RCS is not available. The technical standard behind it is the GSMA Universal Profile, and the agent side is documented in Google's RCS for Business developer documentation.

The WhatsApp side is different in shape: it is a standalone app that customers already have open through the day, upgraded via the API into a multi-agent, automated channel with a shared inbox, approved templates and a verified business profile. Both raise the bar over raw SMS; they just do it in different places on the phone.

Reach is where the app-based channel still leads. WhatsApp Business API reach in India spans both Android and iPhone with near-universal smartphone coverage, which makes it the dependable choice for a campaign that has to hit every customer regardless of handset. RCS coverage is large and growing on Android but effectively limited on iPhone until Apple's rollout matures and operators enable it broadly.

items.title: Cross-platform by default:
items.desc: the app channel lands on Android and iPhone alike, so a nationwide bulk broadcast reaches the whole list.

items.title: Android-strong, iPhone-limited:
items.desc: RCS coverage runs high on Android handsets, common in tier-2 and tier-3 India, but thin on iPhone for now.

items.title: Operator-dependent:
items.desc: RCS availability varies by carrier and device, so real reach is worth checking against your own audience.

items.title: Match reach to the audience:
items.desc: an Android-skewed customer base narrows the gap; a mixed base still favours the cross-platform option.

sections.heading: How Billing Works by Message Category

blocks.html: The two channels price differently, which is why headline rates mislead. On the app side, Meta charges per delivered template message, with the rate set by category — marketing, utility or authentication — and replies to a customer who messaged first are generally free inside the open service window. This is per-message pricing for business channels, not the old per-conversation model. RCS is typically billed per message by the operator or aggregator, and Indian rates are set through those operators rather than a single global card.

items.title: Priced by category:
items.desc: marketing, utility and authentication templates each carry a different per-message rate on the app channel.

items.title: Free replies window:
items.desc: answering a customer who wrote first, within the service window, generally carries no charge on the app side.

items.title: Per-message on RCS:
items.desc: RCS sends are usually charged per message, which can suit high-volume transactional messaging without the free-reply window.

items.title: Compare on real volume:
items.desc: because the models differ, the only fair comparison is your own category mix and send volume, not a single sticker rate.

blocks.html: The official per-category breakdown for the app channel lives in Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform pricing documentation, and Ojiva AI will size both channels against your real campaigns during setup rather than quoting a number that dates quickly.

sections.heading: Rich Cards, Carousels and Interactive Replies

blocks.html: Both channels move well beyond a wall of text, but they lead with different strengths. RCS messaging is built around rich cards and swipeable carousels in the native inbox, while the app channel pairs rich media with mature automation, catalogs and in-thread payments. The rich media messaging features on each are what turn a passive alert into a tap.

items.title: Cards and carousels:
items.desc: both support branded cards and horizontal carousels, so an offer or product set is browsable in the thread.

items.title: Suggested and quick replies:
items.desc: tap-to-respond buttons keep the customer moving without typing, which lifts customer engagement.

items.title: Automation depth:
items.desc: the app channel has mature chatbot flows today; RCS automation is emerging but capable for structured sends.

items.title: Payments in-thread:
items.desc: in-conversation payment is well established on the app side and more limited on RCS for now.

sections.heading: Deliverability and the Trust That Lifts Open Rates

blocks.html: Both channels use a verified sender identity, which is what pushes message deliverability and open rates far above anonymous SMS. A recognised business name and logo tells the customer the message is genuinely from you before they read a word. RCS gets there through the operator-verified sender defined in the GSMA Universal Profile; the app channel gets there through Meta's verified business profile and green tick.

items.title: Verified either way:
items.desc: a verified sender on both channels earns more opens than an unknown number ever will.

items.title: Read receipts and status:
items.desc: delivery and read receipts on both give you real feedback instead of guessing whether a send landed.

items.title: Opt-in keeps you clean:
items.desc: clear opt-in and approved templates keep marketing out of the spam bin and inside the rules.

items.title: Alerts almost always land:
items.desc: RCS with SMS fallback means a time-critical message reaches the customer somewhere, every time.

sections.heading: Getting a Verified Sender Approved on Each Channel

blocks.html: Going live means passing a verification step on either channel, and the two paths are separate. RCS agent verification in India runs through Google and the operators — a brand and agent are registered, reviewed and approved before they can send. The app channel runs through Meta's own Business verification and template review, which is what produces the green verified badge.

items.title: RCS agent onboarding:
items.desc: the sender is registered as a verified agent through Google and the operators before the first branded send.

items.title: Meta business verification:
items.desc: the app channel verifies the business and reviews display name and templates to unlock the green tick.

items.title: Templates reviewed first:
items.desc: on the app side, marketing, utility and authentication templates are approved before they can be broadcast.

items.title: Plan for review time:
items.desc: both approvals take a little lead time, so it pays to start verification before a campaign deadline.

blocks.html: One point trips up almost every business coming from text campaigns, so it is worth stating plainly: DLT registration is a TRAI mechanism specific to SMS. It does not apply to the WhatsApp Business API, which uses Meta's own verification instead, and it is separate from RCS agent onboarding. Consent still matters on every channel and should follow DPDP Act principles — a clear opt-in at capture and an easy opt-out — but the SMS DLT track sits on its own.

For an OTP or a delivery update, what matters is that the message arrives, not that it looks rich. This is where SMS fallback messaging is a real edge: when RCS is unavailable on a handset, the message quietly drops to plain SMS, so a time-critical alert still lands. The app channel has no equivalent fallback — if the customer is not reachable there, the message simply waits.

items.title: Automatic drop to SMS:
items.desc: RCS falls back to SMS on its own, which suits OTPs and transactional messaging that cannot be missed.

items.title: Right for time-sensitive sends:
items.desc: order, delivery and authentication alerts favour the channel that guarantees a landing.

items.title: Richer when supported:
items.desc: where RCS is available the same alert arrives as a branded, tappable card instead of a grey text.

items.title: App channel for engagement:
items.desc: the app side stays the stronger home for two-way support and marketing, not last-mile fallback.

sections.heading: Turning Conversations Into Orders and Payments

blocks.html: Where a channel earns its keep is in closing the loop from interest to purchase. As a conversational commerce channel, the app side is ahead today: a customer can browse a catalog, place an order and pay without leaving the thread, and receive order and delivery updates in the same place. RCS is building toward the same, and already handles rich, tappable prompts well.

items.title: Catalog in the chat:
items.desc: the app channel lets customers browse products in-thread, so questions and buying happen in one window.

items.title: Order and pay in place:
items.desc: adding items and paying inside the conversation closes the sale while interest is still high.

items.title: Updates that reassure:
items.desc: confirmations and delivery notes arrive where the customer will actually see them.

items.title: Two-way support:
items.desc: mature chatbot and agent handoff make the app side strong for guidance, not just one-way sends.

sections.heading: When an Android-First Audience Changes the Maths

blocks.html: The verdict shifts with your customer base. For Android-first business messaging — an audience skewed to Android handsets, heavy on transactional sends like OTPs and delivery alerts — RCS can be both cheaper per message and more certain to land thanks to its SMS fallback. For anything needing cross-platform reach, two-way support or in-thread commerce, the app channel still wins.

The strongest setups do not choose once and forget it: they run the app channel for engagement, marketing and commerce, and keep RCS or SMS as a transactional layer underneath. That is how you get conversations that convert without paying for reach or richness you do not need. Book a demo and Ojiva AI will model the split for your own volumes.

It is not a winner-takes-all decision — the best stacks run both, each doing the job it is strongest at, on one verified footing.

items.q: Is RCS better than WhatsApp Business API for business in India?
items.a: Not for most businesses. The app channel reaches customers on both Android and iPhone with mature tooling and conversational commerce, so it is the safer primary choice. RCS is Android-strong and still early on business tooling, but its automatic SMS fallback makes it excellent for Android-heavy transactional messaging like OTPs and delivery alerts.

items.q: What is the difference between RCS and WhatsApp Business API?
items.a: The app channel is a standalone app with cross-platform reach and per-message billing by category. RCS is the upgraded successor to SMS built into the native Android Messages app, needs no install, and drops back to plain SMS when unavailable — but it has limited iPhone support and newer business tooling. Both use a verified sender, so both beat anonymous SMS on trust.

items.q: Is RCS cheaper than WhatsApp for high-volume sends?
items.a: It can be for high-volume transactional sends. RCS is usually billed per message and is often positioned below marketing rates on the app channel, but the app side offers free replies to customers who message first, which RCS does not. Because the pricing models differ, compare on your real volume and category mix rather than a headline rate.

items.q: Does RCS work on iPhone in India?
items.a: Support is rolling out but still inconsistent. Until Apple's RCS implementation matures and operators enable it broadly, RCS reach on iPhone in India is limited — which is a key reason the WhatsApp Business API remains the stronger cross-platform choice for a mixed audience.

items.q: Can I use both RCS and WhatsApp Business API together?
items.a: Often that is the strongest setup. Run the app channel for marketing, support and commerce, and keep RCS or SMS as a transactional fallback layer for Android-first alerts. They serve different jobs, so it is rarely an either-or decision. Ojiva AI runs both from one dashboard so you can split traffic sensibly.

items.q: How does RCS agent verification work in India?
items.a: A brand and its messaging agent are registered and reviewed through Google and the operators before any branded sends go out. This is separate from the app channel's Meta business verification, and separate again from the SMS DLT process. A provider like Ojiva AI handles the onboarding so you are not navigating operator requirements alone.

items.q: Is DLT registration required for RCS in India?
items.a: DLT is a TRAI mechanism specific to SMS, so it is not the same track as RCS. RCS uses its own agent verification through Google and the operators, and the WhatsApp Business API uses Meta's business verification. Consent and opt-out still matter on every channel and should follow DPDP Act principles, but DLT itself applies to SMS.

items.q: How much does RCS messaging cost per message in India?
items.a: RCS is typically billed per message through the operator or aggregator, and Indian rates are set that way rather than by a single global card.
